title: Repair Charge Schedule and Repair Shop Turnaround — Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program
content:
Repair schedule of the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program, stating per usage type what is charged for repairs of district-owned instruments and how long the district's contracted repair shop takes.

**Kinds of repair.** A minor repair caused by mishandling is one such as pads, corks, valve or slide alignment, or bridge or string replacement. A major repair caused by mishandling is one such as dents, a cracked body, or a broken neck or seam. Normal wear found at return is a separate line.

| Usage type | Minor repair caused by mishandling (USD) | Major repair caused by mishandling (USD) | Normal wear found at return (USD) | Calendar days the repair shop takes | Loaner instrument issued during repair |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Percussion Equipment Usage | 20.00 | 85.00 | 0.00 | 10 | yes |
| Woodwind Instrument Usage | 45.00 | 225.00 | 0.00 | 10 | yes |
| Brass Instrument Usage | 40.00 | 210.00 | 0.00 | 10 | yes |
| Orchestra String Instrument Usage | 35.00 | 180.00 | 0.00 | 10 | yes |
| Large Instrument Usage (Tuba, Cello, String Bass) | 55.00 | 320.00 | 0.00 | 10 | yes |
| Summer Instrument Checkout | 45.00 | 225.00 | 0.00 | 10 | no |

## Reading the schedule

- The charge for normal wear is 0.00 under every usage type.
- The repair shop takes 10 calendar days under every usage type.
- A loaner instrument is issued during repair under the five school-year usage types; under Summer Instrument Checkout no loaner is issued.
- The largest minor and major repair charges are those of Large Instrument Usage (Tuba, Cello, String Bass), 55.00 and 320.00; the smallest are those of Percussion Equipment Usage, 20.00 and 85.00.

Hypothetical illustration: a bassoon held under Woodwind Instrument Usage that needs new pads because of mishandling is a minor repair at 45.00; the same bassoon with a cracked body is a major repair at 225.00.
